src: APPSC Group-II Mains 2025
s: Telugu Ganga Canal Water is supplied to which of the following states?
x:
The Telugu Ganga Project is an inter-state water project designed primarily to supply drinking water to Chennai (Tamil Nadu) while also providing irrigation benefits to Andhra Pradesh. The project utilizes surplus waters of the Krishna River and conveys them through a network of reservoirs and canals. Water flows through Srisailam Reservoir, Somasila Reservoir, Kandaleru Reservoir, and finally reaches Poondi Reservoir near Chennai. Apart from supplying drinking water to Chennai, the project also provides irrigation facilities to drought-prone districts of Rayalaseema and parts of Nellore district. The project is an example of interstate cooperation involving Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu. However, the state receiving drinking water under the project is Tamil Nadu. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).
Exam Note:
• Purpose – Drinking water supply to Chennai
• Beneficiary State – Tamil Nadu
• Major Reservoirs – Srisailam, Somasila, Kandaleru

s:
Consider the following rivers:
1. Vamsadhara
2. Indravati
3. Pranahita
4. Pennar
Which of the above are tributaries of Godavari?
x: Indravati and Pranhita are tributaries of the Godavari. The Godavari basin extends over Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha, as well as smaller parts of Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, and Puducherry. The Godavari basin is the second-largest basin in India.The River rises from Trimbakeshwar in the Nashik district of Maharashtra. It is the largest peninsular Indian river that drains into the Bay of Bengal. It divides into two main streams, the Gautami Godavari on the east and the Vashishta Godavari on the west and forms a large delta before it pours into the Bay of Bengal. The delta of the Godavari is lobate, with a rounded bulge and numerous distributaries. • Important cities: Nashik, Paithan, Nizamabad, Rajahmundry, etc., • Right bank tributaries: Pravara, Manjira, and Maner. • Left bank tributaries: Purna, Pranahita, Indravathi, and Sabari Indian Geography PMF IAS Geo – 83 • Indravati River: It flows through the states of Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and Andhra Pradesh in India. It originates in the Eastern Ghats in the Kalahandi district of Odisha and flows for a distance of 535 kilometres before joining the Godavari River at Bhadrachalam in Telangana. • Pranahita: It flows through the states of Maharashtra, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh in India. It joins the Godavari River at Khammam in Telangana. Vamsadhara is incorrect: The Vamsadhara River flows through the states of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh. It originates in the Eastern Ghats in the Kalahandi district of Odish
